subject.declared_domain: NFRA_MSGRAPH S2: ingests the Microsoft doc-cloud (SharePoint + OneDrive STRUCTURE / METADATA / ACTIVITY) into the shared globgrph graph as an additive MS_CLOUD node class plus MS edges. The manifest names it as materializer of the part `ms_heat_snap`. ⛔ THIS FILE HAS NO WRITE PRIMITIVE OF ITS OWN -- it mutates an in-memory dict and returns; see location.

methodology.how: A best-effort FOLD, not a standalone job. derive_runner.main() calls extract_ms_cloud(graph, ...) alongside its sibling folds; the function appends the MS nodes as classes_data['MS_CLOUD'] and the MS edges to graph['edges'], then returns. It NEVER refactors, mutates or drops an AWS node, and when MS is disabled (the default) the graph is returned BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the AWS-only derive is unchanged. Emitted shape matches the existing globgrph convention -- fixed node keys {id, arn, type, name, layer, drift_class} with every other key auto-flowing to the additive props column, so there is no silent drop. Source access is confined to four document-storage gateway tools by an allowlist, and a second fail-closed layer certifies the emit itself.

composes.note: the caller; this module is a fold inside its main(), not an entry point

invents.note: MS nodes carry layer='ms', source='ms', drift_class=<ms_state>; additive to the AWS graph, never a refactor of it
the SS4 emit-time catastrophic-floor cert, raising MsContentCommsLeak on four distinct leak shapes

coverage.denominator_absent_reason: NOT MEASURED BY THIS CARD. The emitted node count is a run-time property of the live MS tenant and of the exclusion set, and running the fold would require the gateway plus MS enabled -- which is off by default. A ceiling is a bound, not a denominator, and quoting 8000 as the coverage denominator would be exactly the substitution this field exists to prevent.

key.identity_space: globgrph node ids in the shared graph namespace, with MS nodes distinguished by layer='ms' and source='ms' rather than by a separate id space.
key.key_expression: The node dict's `id`, minted per node type by the builders _site_node :268, _drive_node :286, _item_node :305, _user_node :340, and edges by _edge :353 over (src_id, dst_id, edge_type). A consumer computes a member's key by reading that field; it is the same `id` key the AWS nodes use, which is the point of the additive design -- MS nodes join the existing namespace rather than opening a second one.
key.declared_mapping: MS nodes carry the same fixed key set as AWS nodes ({id, arn, type, name, layer, drift_class}) with layer='ms' as the discriminator, so the mapping between the MS origin space and the graph node space is the builder functions themselves. There is no declared table and no reverse mapping from a graph id back to a Graph API object beyond what the builders encode.
key.evidence: key_expression MEASURED at source -- the five builder functions and the fixed-key convention are read directly (:268, :286, :305, :340, :353, docstring :14-17). key_is_stable is 'unknown' and marked HELD rather than measured: MS item ids come from the Graph API, and whether a SharePoint or OneDrive item id survives a move, rename or re-provision is a property of Microsoft's service that I did not test and that the source does not assert. Recording 'stable' here would be a guess about someone else's identity guarantees, which is precisely what v3.1 forbids for a key.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: IT RAISES AND FAILS THE WHOLE DERIVE CLOSED. assert_no_content_comms :139-150 is an emit-time certificate that raises MsContentCommsLeak on four distinct leak shapes: a node_type outside the allowlist, a node field KEY matching a forbidden content/comms substring, a node web_url or path resolving to a comms surface, and an edge_type outside the allowlist. It returns None only on a clean structural-only emit. This is the CTO catastrophic-floor invariant, and it is fail-closed by design: a leak stops the derive rather than committing a graph.
silent_degrade_paths: THE FOLD IS BEST-EFFORT AND ITS ABSENCE IS INVISIBLE. When MS is disabled -- the DEFAULT -- the graph is returned byte-identical, which is exactly right for the AWS derive and means a consumer cannot tell 'MS is off' from 'MS ran and found nothing' by looking at the graph. The two states differ only in whether the MS_CLOUD class exists at all.

MS_NODE_CEILING silently bounds the emit at 8000 by default. A tenant larger than the ceiling produces a truncated MS_CLOUD class that is well-formed and incomplete; nothing in the emitted shape records that the ceiling bound it.

The exclusion set removes paths by design, and excluded_path_reason returns the reason -- but the reason lives in the run, not in the graph, so an excluded subtree and an absent subtree look identical to a downstream reader.
failure_mode.evidence: assert_no_content_comms :139-150 read in full, including all four raise conditions and the docstring naming it 'the gate-impossible leg'. 'distinguishable_from_true_negative: YES' is measured on the PRIMARY failure -- a content/comms leak cannot pass quietly because the cert raises and the derive fails -- and it is backed by a named adversarial artifact rather than by the code alone: tests/test_ms_cloud_cert.py is the inject->FAIL / clean->PASS regression the docstring calls the catastrophic-floor acceptance artifact (CTO binding condition 1). A cert with a passing-and-failing pair is a control that has been shown to fire, which is a stronger claim than a guard that merely exists. The three degrade paths above are the honest qualification and are each about COMPLETENESS, never about leakage.

verdict.why: The strongest failure mode in this population of four: a fail-closed emit-time certificate covering four leak shapes, backed by a named adversarial regression that has been shown to fire in both directions -- not a guard that merely exists. The additive-only contract is real and testable (byte-identical graph when disabled), and the four-tool source allowlist means the catastrophic floor is enforced at two independent layers rather than one. Three qualifications, none of them about leakage. (1) IT WRITES NOTHING: zero write primitives over 656 lines, so the manifest's attribution of `ms_heat_snap` to this file does not resolve to a writer of those bytes -- `snap_store.py` registers and appends that surface. The consistent reading is that `generation.materializer` is not uniformly at (file, write-path) grain; for this part it names a data origin. I did NOT trace this module's MS nodes to ms_heat_snap rows, so that link is unverified here. (2) Its trigger is inherited from derive_runner, a component I did not card -- actual_trigger is held, not measured. (3) The key is a Graph API id whose stability across move/rename is Microsoft's guarantee, not one this card can assert; key_is_stable is 'unknown' and held.
